svg.text: Volume sensor wiring: HC-SR04 to Raspberry Pi 4 (female-to-male wires only)
Seen from above. Unplug the Pi first. Female ends go on the Pi and the sensor; male ends into the breadboard. Holes a–e in one column are connected.

g.text: pin 1 = square pad, end farthest from USB
Unplug the Pi. Push the two resistors into the breadboard: 1 kΩ (brown-black-red) c9 → c13, 2 kΩ (red-black-red) d13 → d17.
Sensor VCC → e3. Sensor Trig → e6. Sensor Echo → e9. Sensor GND → e17. (female end on the sensor pin)
Pi pin 2 (5V) → a3. Pi pin 16 (GPIO 23) → a6. Pi pin 18 (GPIO 24) → a13. Pi pin 6 (GND) → a17.
Check: nothing from the sensor goes into column 13; only the Pi's pin 18 and the two resistors meet there.
Never put the sensor's Echo straight onto a Pi pin: it sends 5 V. The resistors bring it down to about 3.3 V.
Power on, then run .venv/bin/python volume_sensor.py and hold your hand 5–35 cm above the sensor.
8 female-to-male wires, 2 resistors. No 2 kΩ? Two 1 kΩ in a row work the same. The breadboard's power rails aren't used. Resistors have no + or −: either way round is fine.
